title: A Dark Sky Full of Light
caption: The VLT Survey Telescope under the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: In this high-resolution panorama of ESO's Paranal Observatory, the VLT Survey Telescope (VST) and its dome hold centre stage in the foreground, beneath the Milky Way's arc. Many nebulae are scattered along our galaxy's arc and the area around the constellation Orion, at lower right.

Above the VLT Unit Telescope glows the Large Magellanic Cloud, one of the Milky Way's satellite galaxies. Although the Atacama sky is usually dark, faint, colourful airglow often brightens it, particularly close to the horizon.

ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek took the image on 4 April 2016. The picture's title, A Dark Sky Full of Light, sums up the scene: a sky that is typically dark, yet here is crowded with glowing nebulae, galaxies and airglow.

understand.summary: This is a high-resolution ground-based panorama by Petr Horálek; the packet does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: Airglow and many of the nebulae are faint, and a camera gathering light over time shows them more clearly than the eye would.

alt: A telescope dome in the foreground under the arc of the Milky Way, with nebulae along the arc, a fuzzy patch above a larger telescope, and coloured glow near the horizon.
